pages.visible_text: Debrecen, Hungary - 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-16 Methods And Data Transparent baselines, explainable regime rules, source notes, and downloadable outputs for the current report. Climatological Reference Ledger Metric This period 1991-2020 mean (anomaly) Recent 10-year mean (anomaly) 1990-present percentile Temperature 25.5 22.0 (+3.4) 23.8 (+1.7) 78th Precipitation 0.0 6.5 (-6.5) 4.5 (-4.5) 19th Wind 4.7 3.9 (+0.8) 3.9 (+0.9) 86th Pressure 1017.7 1014.3 (+3.4) 1015.3 (+2.4) 78th Cloud 6.3 42.6 (-36.3) 40.1 (-33.7) 3th Solar radiation 19788.0 15440.4 (+4347.6) 16128.3 (+3659.7) 100th Classification Signals above-normal radiation reduced cloudiness limited rainfall Sources And Quality HungaroMet supplies Debrecen Airport observations, composite radar, LINET lightning and Meteosat imagery. Open-Meteo supplies the continuous gridded surface record, pressure-level model fields, synoptic grid, the wide-domain 850 hPa wind field the back-trajectory integrates through, land fields and ERA5 climate archive. Standard normals use 1991-2020; the recent comparison retains the prior 10 years and is stored in baseline_metrics.csv. Data completeness check passed with 72/72 expected local-period hours. Hungary-wide electricity context from Energy-Charts (primarily ENTSO-E data). Model-derived atmospheric profile near Debrecen; it is not an observed radiosonde. Dew point is calculated from model temperature and relative humidity. HungaroMet station 64711 (Debrecen Airport); 10-minute observations. Station coverage: 300/432 expected records (69%). HungaroMet 1 km composite radar sampled every 30 minutes; 128/144 frames available (89%). The browser replay uses every 60 minutes and a 3 km display grid for practical loading. Accumulation is a reflectivity-derived Z-R estimate and should be treated as a spatial precipitation proxy. HungaroMet LINET events within 150 km of Debrecen. Detected 0 lightning events in the reporting period. HungaroMet Meteosat Second Generation RGB and infrared products; frames sampled approximately every 180 minutes. Satellite imagery is synchronized by nearest timestamp with radar and LINET timelines, not spatially overlaid. Frontal passages are objective candidates based on three-hour pressure, temperature, wind and precipitation changes. A pressure, precipitation or strong-gust anchor is required to suppress ordinary diurnal temperature and wind cycles. The detector identifies local passage signatures; it does not replace a manually analysed synoptic front. Phenomena are deterministic candidates based on explicit thresholds; they are not manually quality-controlled reports. Observed station evidence is preferred, with gridded or model-derived evidence identified when observations are unavailable. Analogs are selected from 15 years of ERA5 daily data within +/-45 calendar days. Similarity uses standardized temperature, precipitation, wind, radiation, cloud and pressure; it is descriptive rather than predictive. Synoptic fields are model analyses from Open-Meteo Historical Forecast data. Frames are sampled every 6 hours on a 1-degree Central European grid. Vorticity, thermal advection and kinematic frontogenesis are finite-difference diagnostics derived on the reporting grid. A true 2-PVU dynamical-tropopause surface is not exposed by the no-secret provider and is not approximated. Standard anomalies use 30 same-calendar ERA5 periods from 1991-2020. Full-record percentiles use 36 same-calendar periods from 1990-2025. The recent-climate comparison uses 10 periods and remains separate from the WMO standard-normal window. Rolling soil, VPD and ET0 fields use Open-Meteo Historical Weather best-match gridded data, not station measurements. The 1991-2020 water-balance reference is fixed to ERA5; the rolling best-match series can use newer IFS and ERA5/ERA5-Land inputs. Water balance is precipitation minus FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration and does not include runoff or irrigation. Dry/wet context uses the 1991-2020 distribution of same-calendar water-balance windows. PV yield models a south-facing 35-degree fixed array per installed kWp using plane-of-array irradiance and cell-temperature derating. Wind output uses observed/modelled 100 m wind, moist-air density correction, and a generic 3/12/25 m/s cut-in/rated/cut-out power curve. These are reference-system weather yields, not metered production or a forecast. Reanalysis Verification Hourly ERA5 values against Debrecen Airport over the same hours. Bias is reanalysis minus station, so a positive figure means the reanalysis read high. Over 50 paired hours the reanalysis ran 0.89 °C above the instrument on temperature, with a typical absolute miss of 1.31 °C. pages.title: Atlas
pages.visible_text: Debrecen meteorological record Atlas What kind of weather did Debrecen just have, how unusual was it, and what did it imply for solar and wind energy potential? Atlas is a deterministic weather diary for Debrecen. It combines airport observations, remote sensing, gridded climate records, atmospheric diagnostics, historical analogs and physically based renewable-energy estimates in two regularly updated publications. Current publications DAILY / PUBLIC Daily Public Report The last complete local day, with a concise weather account, objective events, renewable yield and climate context. Latest edition 2026-08-16 → 72 HOURS / EXPERT Meteorological Analysis Surface, synoptic, satellite, radar, upper-air, land-surface, climate and energy diagnostics for the latest complete period. Current window 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-16 → PRESERVED RECORD Report Archive Saved daily reports, rolling analyses and legacy weekly editions, presented in the current Atlas reading environment. Browse history Open archive → Evidence, not decoration The report begins with what was observed and labels every gridded, remotely sensed or model-derived contribution. Interactive figures support inspection, while deterministic text records the thresholds and evidence behind each interpretation. OBS HungaroMet Debrecen Airport REMOTE Radar + LINET + Meteosat GRID Open-Meteo + ERA5 MODEL Column diagnostics + renewable yield Geographic scope Debrecen, Hungary Climate reference 1991-2020 standard normal, recent decade and full record Publication cadence Daily public record and rolling 72-hour analysis Scientific frame Atlas is descriptive, diagnostic, climatological and energy-oriented. It is not forecast calibration, an operational warning service or a plant-level production forecast. Open data The pipeline uses public HungaroMet, Open-Meteo and Energy-Charts endpoints without repository secrets. Optional-source failures remain explicitly unavailable rather than becoming false zeroes. Project notes Methods, source provenance and implementation details are maintained in the Atlas repository . Every analytical page includes its own evidence notes and machine-readable downloads.

Publication The public report is rebuilt daily from the last complete Europe/Budapest calendar day. Open-Meteo supplies continuous gridded surface fields, model pressure levels and ERA5 climate fields. Optional-source failures are reported as unavailable, never treated as observed zeroes. Climate references "Normal" means the 1991-2020 ERA5 standard reference. The recent-decade comparison and full-record percentile are shown separately.
